title: Maryam above the women of the worlds
hookLine: the angels say Allah has chosen and purified her (3:42–43)

cards: Readers of the Qur'an point something out about Maryam: a queen appears in it, and prophets' wives and mothers, but tradition counts her as the one woman the book calls by her own name.

A whole surah, the nineteenth, carries it. And here in Al 'Imran, the girl Zakariyya was raising has grown up, and the angels speak to her directly, with words that set her above the women of the worlds.

teach.b: In 3:42 the angels say: O Maryam, God has chosen you and purified you, and chosen you above the women of the worlds. Listen to the shape of it.
Chosen, istafa, the word from two days ago with the family of Imran, comes twice.

Commentators explain the two choosings differently: some say the first is being chosen for devotion and accepted in the sanctuary, and the second is being chosen above all women, for the birth of Isa.
Between them, purified: kept clean of what would stain her.

Then 3:43 gives her the instructions any worshiper gets: be devoutly obedient to your Lord, prostrate, and bow with those who bow. A young woman, alone in a sanctuary, addressed by angels, and told to pray.
Verse 44 adds a scene from her childhood: the men of the temple cast their pens, like drawing lots, to decide who would care for her, and argued over the honor. Zakariyya won.
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is reported, in Sahih al-Bukhari, to have said that the best of the women of her time was Maryam, and the best of the women of his own time was Khadijah, his wife.
A hadith in Tirmidhi names four women who are enough, among all the women of the world, to look to: Maryam, Asiya the wife of Pharaoh, Khadijah, and Fatimah his daughter.

teach.h: ABOVE THE WOMEN OF THE WORLDS.
teach.b: Christians honor her too, as Mary, and the two traditions tell her story in their own ways. In the Qur'an's telling, her greatness isn't fame. It's two choosings, one purifying, and a life of bowing in prayer.

how: Muslims hold Maryam in deep honor as the mother of the prophet Isa and, following the hadith, among the best of women; Surah Maryam (19) and her verses in Al 'Imran are recited and taught, and girls are often named after her.

s: a whole surah of the Qur'an carries Maryam's name
the word chosen appears once in 3:42
it comes twice: chosen, purified, and chosen above the women of the worlds.
the angels told her to pray and bow
3:43: be devout, prostrate, and bow with those who bow.

games.q: Maryam is a child, and the men of the temple all want to care for her. how do they decide?
o: they cast their pens, like drawing lots.
games.why: they cast their pens (3:44), arguing over the honor, and Zakariyya became her guardian.

practice: Bring to mind a woman of faith you've known or read about, a grandmother who prayed before dawn, a teacher, a neighbor, someone from history, and picture her at prayer, or doing the one thing she did faithfully, year after year.
Let yourself feel some honor for her, and if you pray, ask God's mercy on her.

wordCard.voice: Maryam, the mother of Isa: chosen, purified, and chosen again, in the words of the angels in 3:42. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Maryam, Mary; the name of the Qur'an's nineteenth surah.
